key_insight: Diamond–silicon nitride sliding exhibits two regimes: interface-localized shear linked to interfacial bond density, and shear within the softer material dominated by adhesion from full interfacial bonding.
engineering_relevance: Controlling diamond passivation, surface orientation and load could help manage friction and wear in ceramic contacts and polishing applications.
method: Train a reactive machine learning potential for C/H/N/O/Si structures, surfaces, interfaces and environmental molecules.
Evaluate diamond surface reaction barriers and amorphous silicon nitride and silica properties.
Simulate diamond–silicon nitride sliding across four diamond orientations, clean and H/OH-passivated surfaces, and loads of 0.1–23 GPa.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports training on a large, diverse structural dataset and testing against ab initio reaction barriers and structural/mechanical properties, but gives no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Transferability to environments and wear processes beyond the tested structures and sliding conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Development and application of a machine learning potential for diamond surfaces and their sliding interfaces with silicon nitride and silica: effect of passivation, orientation and load
